audit.framework_rationale: TensorCircuit is used for circuit construction, gates, statevector generation, expectation values, reduced density matrices, and Renyi entropy. JAX supplies TensorCircuit's backend, differentiation, JIT compilation, and optimizer arithmetic; NumPy supplies constants, initialization, and returned arrays. Neither is used to implement a raw end-to-end quantum simulator.
audit.cheating_rationale: The submission does not hardcode benchmark outputs, read hidden answers, modify tests or reward files, or exploit evaluator behavior. Its fixed random seed only makes the required Gaussian initialization reproducible.
audit.fidelity_rationale: The implementation prepares |010101010101>, constructs three even-plus-odd blocks with separate rotations and XX/YY/ZZ interaction parameters, uses 243 trainable scalars, measures Renyi-2 entropy after each complete block, evaluates the specified open-boundary XXZ Hamiltonian and staggered field, applies the configured entropy penalty, performs exactly the configured number of Adam updates without early stopping, records metrics immediately before every update, and returns all required NumPy histories with the required shapes.
audit.implementation_error_rationale: No obvious implementation error is present. Parameter counting, bond ranges, Hamiltonian signs and coefficients, checkpoint placement, entropy MSE, Adam bias correction, and pre-update history recording are consistent with the specification and the reported evaluation passed all criteria.
